This widening reflects increasing uncertainty over time. There are, of course, risks or events that could push the actual outcomes outside the given intervals. Sudden shocks—like geopolitical turmoil, extreme weather events, major policy changes, or unforeseen news—can cause outcomes to spike or crash well beyond predicted ranges, especially at longer horizons. Additionally, if the model used to generate the forecast has systematically underestimated the potential for larger fluctuations or was calibrated using atypical historical data, extreme deviations could occur. Ultimately, there’s always a chance the complex interplay of factors in any real-world system could lead to outcomes that differ significantly from even the best-informed predictions.
